paper_metadata.title: Fabrication of Ni-Based Superalloys Containing Nb and Their High Temperature Oxidation Behaviors

evidence.quote: Ni-based superalloys with different contents of Nb addition were fabricated by vacuum melting and casting.

other.equipment: vacuum arc melting furnace equipped with an induction stir

evidence.quote: The Ni-based superalloys were manufactured by vacuum melting. A vacuum arc melting furnace equipped with an induction stir was used in this study.
After normalizing (1200 C, 4 h) and aging (800 C, 10 h) in pure argon, specimens (10 mm 10 mm 3 mm) were cut from the ingots.
After normalizing (1200 C, 4 h) and aging (800 C, 10 h) in pure argon, specimens (10 mm 10 mm 3 mm) were cut from the ingots.
All the specimens were mechanically abraded to remove the oxides on their surface. In order to guarantee the surface uniformity of all the specimens, the same grade abrasive paper (800 #) was used.

The high temperature oxidation test was carried out according to the Chinese National Aviation Standard (HB 5258-2000, test method for determination of oxidation resistance of steel and superalloy). Thermogravimetry was used to study the oxidation kinetics. A traditional chamber electric furnace was employed to carry out the oxidation test at 800 C for 100 h.

evidence.quote: The oxide scale thickness is about 13.3 mm on specimen A (Ni–Cr–M alloy). The scale can be divided into three layers, i.e., a loose outer layer (TiO2, NiO, and NiCr2O4), a middle layer with dense Cr2O3, and an internal layer (TiO2 and Al2O3)

evidence.quote: The oxide scale formed on specimen B (Ni–Cr–2.0%Nb–M alloy) is about 7.7 mm and is dense and uniform in the cross section as observed in Fig. 5(b).
